data.title: Organisational Data Present in Paste Sites and Threat Vendor Corpora
data.summary:
Data relating to the organisation — credentials, internal documents and infrastructure
detail — is present in paste sites, leak aggregators and commercial threat intelligence
corpora accessible to third parties.
data.description:
Material that reaches these corpora is effectively permanent and is indexed for retrieval
by exactly the search terms an adversary would use. Removal is generally not available;
what is available is knowing what is there.

Organisations frequently learn of such exposure only when it is used. Where the
organisation does not search these sources itself, an adversary has a standing advantage of
whatever the collection interval would have been.

The same corpora are available to defenders, and monitoring them is one of the few
collection activities that is unambiguously lawful and low-cost.
data.recommendation:
* Monitor paste sites and leak aggregators for the organisation's domains, product names
  and executive names on a schedule.
* Treat anything found as compromised rather than as an item to request removal of.
* Feed discovered credentials directly into a forced reset process rather than into a
  report that waits for review.
data.short_recommendation: Monitor leak corpora on a schedule and treat findings as compromised.
